sentences.text:
Shri Vishal Sharma, learned counsel for the appella  Shri Pradip Kumar Gupta with Shri Bhashkar Agrawal,
 counsel for the respondent No.3.
 ORDER Heard on I.A. No.8445/2023.
With consent of the parties also heard finally.

The learned counsel for the appellants has explained in extensive the circumstances, which were prevailing for not filing the appeal in time keeping in view the fact that there is no reply on behalf of any of the respondents although there is oral objection to the application, delay of 509 days in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.
However, this period of delay shall be excluded while applying interest in case, compensation is enhanced.
2 The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 22.02.2022 passed in MACC No.80/2022.
The challenge is to the quantification of compensation.

3. The liability of the insurance company is not under dispute, hence, the 2 MA-6641-2023 appeal is being heard finally in absence of owner and driver.
4.

The short facts of the case are that on 07.08.2020 at around 05:00 in the evening a boy Yash was standing beside the canal at Bagwaan- Madraaniya Road and a motorcycle at the said time was coming from Madraaniya side which was bearing registration number MP10-MZ-3846.
The rider of the said motorcycle was riding the same in a rash and negligent manner, thus, it got rammed into the standing boy who sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to them.
5. The appellants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Yash, the said boy.
The claims tribunal after recording evidence concluded that it was the fault of the rider of the insured vehicle, thus, a total compensation of Rs.5,24,500/- was awarded.
The claims tribunal applied a multiplier of 20 on notional income of Rs.15,000/- per annum, thus, the compensation was arrived at.
6. Learned counsel for the appellants prays and submits that the income of the deceased boy should be enhanced and consequential compensation should also be enhanced.

sentences.text:
7. Learned counsel for the insurance company was controverting the submissions of the learned counsel for the appellants that considering the facts of the present case, there is no requirement to reassess the income of the deceased boy for the reason that multiplier of 20 has been applied, thus,
if at all there was any deficiency in the assessment of income that has been compensated by applying a multiplier which is much higher than what should 3 MA-6641-2023 have been applied.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.

In the peculiar facts of the present case, considering that on one side the income has been taken on lower side and on the other hand, multiplier has been taken in a substantially higher quotient.
This Court is not inclined to requantify the amount of compensation, however, in order to constitute a just compensation a further amount of Rs.1,75,000/- is awarded in lump sum over and above the amount which has already been awarded by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall be paid to the appellants with an interest @ 6% per annum from the date of the application before the claims tribunal.
10. However, considering the fact that there was delay of 509 days in filing the present appeal, while calculating interest on the enhanced amount, this period of 509 days shall be excluded.
11. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
